title: I built a strategy game solo with AI as the rest of the team, and put my own voice under every AI line. Here's the voice pipeline.
author: MrTactical_
selftext:
SEEDFALL is a strategy game where you play the villain: one seed falls on a living planet and you grow it into a swarm that eats the world, while every nation fights back with armies, walls, air strikes and nukes. It's just me. Here's where AI was and wasn't used.



\*\*AI:\*\*

\- \*\*Code:\*\* written with an AI coding assistant (Claude Code). The design and the testing are mine; I spent five years as a QA tester before this.

\- \*\*Writing:\*\* drafted with AI under my direction, then every line proof-read and corrected by hand.

\- \*\*Voices:\*\* the narrator and four characters, nearly 900 lines, all generated offline on my own PC.



\*\*Not AI:\*\* the planets, swarms and cutscenes are drawn by the game's own code and shaders. The music is CC0 human-composed pieces plus a score built from recorded orchestral samples. The sounds are real recordings. Nothing is generated while you play.



\*\*The voice pipeline (the part I'd most like feedback on):\*\*



1. \*\*Design each voice from text.\*\* Qwen3-TTS VoiceDesign, from descriptions: a cold British mastermind, plus a gang of four (a cult mother, a gangland heavy, a spymaster, a bored clerk of death).

2. \*\*Get the accent right.\*\* VoiceDesign kept drifting American, and I couldn't trust my ears after hundreds of takes, so I scored "how British" with an accent classifier (SpeechBrain CommonAccent). The mastermind came out of VoiceDesign at about 70%. The four gang members wouldn't, so for them: speak the line with a short British clip from Kokoro-82M as the prompt, then use Seed-VC zero-shot to turn it back into the designed voice. Seed-VC keeps the accent and timing and swaps in the voice.

3. \*\*One sentence at a time.\*\* Long lines broke: words cut in half ("mee... t"), gasps at every full stop. Each sentence is now generated on its own, trimmed to the words, checked with Whisper (best of three takes), then joined with a pause that fits the punctuation.

4. \*\*My own voice underneath.\*\* I fine-tuned Seed-VC on a few minutes of my own recordings and convert every line into my voice. Then I pitch-lock it to the original take (Praat PSOLA), keep only the voiced frames, low-pass it at 3 kHz and mix it 4 dB under the main voice. It reads as a hint, not a second speaker, and it's why the swarm sounds like more than one mind. No other real person's voice is used.

5. \*\*Personality pass.\*\* Five voices from one model all had the same rhythm, so each character gets its own pitch range, pause length and pace.



\*\*What I'd tell anyone trying this:\*\*

\- Don't fight a TTS model for an accent; borrow the accent from a small model and convert.

\- Generate per sentence and verify with speech recognition. It catches the broken takes your ears get tired of.

\- Measure things (the accent, the pauses) instead of judging by ear after the hundredth listen.



There's a free demo on itch if you want to hear it in context (link in the comments). I'm curious how others are handling voices: are you layering, converting, or using TTS straight?

comments.author: MrTactical_
